slides.title: It starts with your phone.
slides.text: Your phone holds a {signer}. It can say one thing: “this is really me.” It can't own anything.

slides.title: The signer acts for you.
slides.text: You are an {identity}: a human. Your phone, your laptop and your watch are your signers, your hands. Lose one, add another, and you are still you.

slides.title: Only you can own things.
slides.text: Not your phone, not an app, not a server. Only an identity owns.

slides.title: You write a to-do list.
slides.text: The list keeps changing, so it's a {Doc}. You attach a photo of the leaking tap. The photo will never change, so it's a {Value}.

slides.title: Every Doc and every Value has its own group.
slides.text: The {group} holds the key. Whoever is in the group can open what it guards. Right now, that's only you.

slides.title: You share the list with Mia.
slides.text: You add Mia to the list's group. She sees the whole list.

slides.title: You share one item with the plumber.
slides.text: “Fix the tap” is its own little Doc, with its own group. You add the plumber to that group only. He sees the tap, and nothing else on your list.

slides.title: Groups inside groups.
slides.text: The list's group is a member of the item's group. So Mia sees the item too, without anyone doing anything.

slides.title: The job is done.
slides.text: You take the plumber out, and the group gets a new key. He keeps what he already saw, and sees nothing new.

slides.title: You and Mia start a home.
slides.text: Together you form a {coop}: an identity made of identities. The coop owns the house list. Neither of you owns it alone, and neither of you can lose it.

slides.title: Coops can hold coops.
slides.text: Your street is a coop of homes. A group the street owns reaches every home, and through them every person.
